A production environment is the deployed context serving real users. Its configuration prioritizes secure defaults, optimized builds, controlled logging, protected secrets, and stable hosting rather than developer convenience.

Detailed exception output and development identity keys should not be exposed there. Operational failures should be investigated through protected server logs while clients receive limited error responses.

A production mechanism makes a resource available to a player. It may introduce the resource directly through a source or use a building, character, or facility to gather or convert inputs into usable output.

Production dependencies can create growth, scarcity, or deadlock. The designer must trace required inputs, capacity, timing, ownership, and what happens when a supply is interrupted.

A production rule specifies that one string may be rewritten as another. In a [[Context-Free Grammar]], every production has a single nonterminal on its left side and a string of terminals and nonterminals on its right side.

Applying a production replaces the chosen nonterminal wherever it occurs, independent of surrounding symbols. A sequence of such replacements forms a [[Derivation]].

A production slot is the deployment slot receiving the application's live traffic. Its address, settings, and backing services form the environment against which users exercise the released application.

A slot swap can promote a verified staging deployment into this role. Production-specific connection strings and secrets should remain associated with the live environment rather than being embedded in the artifact.

A production team creates recurring game content through a comparatively stable workflow after mechanics, tools, and budgets have matured. Visual flow, small batches, and measured cycle time help it deliver assets predictably.

The team differs from an exploratory feature team because much of its uncertainty lies in flow and volume rather than discovering a new mechanic. Production evidence should still feed back into design and scope.

A profile divides a row's occurrence counts by that row's total, so long and short texts can be compared by their relative word usage. Correspondence analysis weights the squared difference between two row profiles by the inverse mass of each column. A difference on a rare attribute therefore contributes more than an equal difference on a common one.

This chi-squared distance is appropriate to the frequency table that begins the analysis. The complete factor-space representation preserves it as Euclidean distance, making otherwise awkward weighted relationships easier to inspect and cluster.

A profile score is one judge's rating of one profile case. A set of profile scores forms the criterion vector that a policy-capturing regression attempts to predict from the case attributes.

Scores must be collected across enough varied profiles to reveal the judge's weighting policy. Repeated profiles can also provide evidence about the stability of the judgments.

A program is a set of instructions written in a [[Programming Language]] that describes a computational process. A program can implement one or more [[Algorithm]]s by translating their steps and control structures into executable notation.

Programs and algorithms are not identical. An algorithm must terminate, while a program may intentionally continue running as long as its computer remains operational. A continuously running service is therefore a computational process even when the whole program is not itself one terminating algorithm.

A programming language is an artificial language used to describe computational instructions. Its vocabulary, syntax, and grammar provide notation for operations and for the [[Control Structure|control structures]] that determine the order in which those operations execute.

Writing an [[Algorithm]] in a programming language makes its steps executable by a computer. Different languages may express the same algorithm differently, so the algorithmic method remains distinct from its particular implementation.

A programming paradigm frames computation through a characteristic set of concepts. Imperative programs command procedures, object-oriented programs coordinate encapsulated objects, and functional programs compose transformations of inputs into outputs.

Different paradigms expose different structures in a problem and hide others. Selecting one is therefore a choice about how to think, represent state, and organize interactions—not merely a choice of syntax.

A progression curve maps increases in cost to increases in benefit or power over time. It regulates the rate at which challenges, rewards, attributes, and thresholds change so the player continues to feel advancement.

Linear, polynomial, exponential, logistic, piecewise-linear, and hand-crafted curves create different pacing and psychological effects. The mathematical shape is a starting structure that must be adjusted through the [[Designer Loop]] and [[Playtesting]].

Perceived challenge may follow a zigzag rather than a smooth rise. A new demand can temporarily push the player toward frustration, while mastery and a quieter section create a plateau before the next development.

A progression system organizes how the player's representation, capabilities, knowledge, or status improve over time. It connects short-term actions and rewards to longer-term goals and a continuing sense of achievement.

Progression usually relies on reinforcing loops regulated by thresholds, costs, challenges, or [[Braking Engine|brakes]]. A [[Progression Curve]] coordinates those changes so benefits remain meaningful and attainable without ending the game too quickly.

A progressive web application is a web application enhanced with browser capabilities associated with installed applications, including offline-oriented loading, background service workers, manifest metadata, and home-screen installation.

Its technical baseline includes a [[Secure Origin]], a registered [[Service Worker]] with fetch handling, minimal offline startup behavior, and a valid [[Web App Manifest]]. It remains linkable and delivered through ordinary web technologies.

A projection checkpoint records the last event-stream position successfully applied to a [[Read Model]]. On restart, the [[Projection]] resumes after this position instead of replaying all history. Updating the checkpoint only after the read-side update provides at-least-once processing, so handlers must account for possible duplicates. Keeping the checkpoint in the same storage and transaction as the read model makes their progress consistent and allows both to be discarded together for a clean rebuild.

A projection transforms domain events into a [[Read Model]]. It subscribes to one or more streams, handles the event types relevant to its view, and inserts, updates, or removes read-side records. Because event streams are optimized for aggregate history rather than filtering current state, projections create representations suited to queries. A projection must tolerate restart and repeated delivery, advance its [[Projection Checkpoint]] only after successful processing, and be rebuildable through replay where practical.

A projective AR display casts generated imagery onto physical surfaces. The projector and target geometry must be calibrated so rendered pixels land on the intended locations, turning walls, objects, or work areas into situated displays.

Projection allows unencumbered viewing and can preserve natural collaboration around a shared object. It cannot make surfaces darker, is sensitive to ambient light and material reflectance, and may be blocked by users or other objects that cast shadows.

A projective module P has the lifting property: for every surjection N → M and map P → M, there is a map P → N whose composite is the original map. Maps from P can be lifted across quotients.

Every [[Free Module]] is projective, and a module is projective exactly when it is a [[Direct Summand of a Free Module]]. Short exact sequences ending in a projective module split.

A projective resolution of a module M is an exact sequence ··· → P₂ → P₁ → P₀ → M → 0 in which every Pᵢ is a [[Projective Module]].

It replaces M by modules with a lifting property, allowing functors to be applied and their failure of exactness measured. The shortest possible resolution length is the [[Projective Dimension]].

A promise represents the eventual success or failure of one asynchronous operation. Consumers attach handlers that run when the operation settles instead of blocking while the result is unavailable.

The [[Fetch API]] uses promises. Angular HttpClient instead returns an [[Observable]], which supports stream-oriented composition and framework operators in addition to delivering an HTTP result.

A prompt repository is a managed collection of messages an assistant can present during known interaction states. Entries may include text, prerecorded audio, variants, and metadata about where each prompt applies.

Centralizing prompts supports consistent wording and easier revision. It also lets a [[Dialog Manager]] select among alternate messages instead of embedding user-facing language directly in transition logic.

A pronunciation model describes how words map to sequences of speech sounds. It connects the word hypotheses favored by a [[Statistical Language Model]] with the phonetic evidence scored by an [[Acoustic Model]].

The model may include multiple pronunciations for one spelling to cover accents and ordinary variation. It is often represented as a lexicon whose entries contain [[Phoneme|phoneme]] sequences.

A proof by contrapositive establishes p → q by directly proving the equivalent implication ¬q → ¬p. It is useful when assuming p does not expose a path to q but the negation of q has a concrete structural form.

The technique depends on the logical equivalence between a [[Conditional Proposition]] and its contrapositive. It differs from [[Proof by Contradiction]], which assumes the negation of the entire claim and derives an impossibility.

A proper [[Ideal]] p is prime when ab ∈ p implies a ∈ p or b ∈ p. Equivalently, the [[Quotient Ring]] R/p is an [[Integral Domain]].

Prime ideals form the points of the [[Spectrum of a Ring]]. They also control radicals, localization, dimension, and primary decomposition. Every [[Maximal Ideal]] is prime because a field is an integral domain.

The source proves the quotient characterization alongside maximal ideals: a proper ideal is prime exactly when its quotient has no zero divisors. This supplies a structural test that avoids checking the product condition directly.

A proper ideal is an ideal not equal to the whole ring. In a ring with identity, an ideal is proper exactly when it does not contain a unit.

Prime and maximal ideals are required to be proper so their quotients remain nontrivial.

A proper ideal q is primary when xy ∈ q and x ∉ q imply that some positive power of y belongs to q. Equivalently, every [[Zero Divisor]] in R/q is [[Nilpotent Element|nilpotent]].

The radical √q of a primary ideal is a [[Prime Ideal]]. Primary ideals act like prime powers in a decomposition, retaining multiplicity information that a radical alone discards.

A proper rational function is a quotient of polynomials whose numerator has lower degree than its denominator. If the numerator's degree is at least as large, [[Polynomial Long Division]] first separates a polynomial part and a proper remainder. Properness is the starting condition for [[Partial Fraction Decomposition]].

A proper submodule N of a finitely generated module M is primary when rm ∈ N with m ∉ N forces a positive power of r to send all of M into N.

The radical of the ideal (N:M) is a [[Prime Ideal]] p, and N is called p-primary. The quotient M/N is then a [[Primary Module]].

A proportion power calculation plans a comparison involving one or two proportions. Its effect measure reflects the expected difference in prevalence, and its sample-size arguments may assume equal groups or permit one group size to be fixed.

The unequal-group form is useful when the number of outcome-positive observations is constrained by the available data. A small prevalence difference or severe imbalance can require a much larger comparison group to maintain the desired power.

A proportional controller responds to present error, a derivative term responds to the error's rate of change, and an integral term accumulates persistent past error. Combined PID control can reduce steady offset while damping overshoot and oscillation. In a multirotor, the resulting commands change individual rotor speeds to achieve the desired position and attitude described by [[Drone Rotation Matrices]].

A proportional symbol map places a symbol at each location and varies its area continuously with a quantitative attribute. Circles are common because their areas can be scaled without implying orientation. The map preserves individual locations while enabling magnitude comparison, but overlapping symbols and imperfect area judgment limit precision. [[Symbol Area Scaling]] defines the mathematical relationship, while [[Perceptual Symbol Scaling]] can adjust it for human underestimation.

A proposition is in disjunctive normal form when it is an OR of AND clauses whose terms are variables or negated variables. Each true row of a [[Truth Table]] supplies one conjunction: use the variable when the row assigns true and its negation when the row assigns false.

Taking the disjunction of these row clauses produces a formula with exactly the table's output behavior. This construction shows that AND, OR, and NOT gates can implement any Boolean input-output table used by a [[Electronic Circuits|combinatorial logic circuit]].

A protected constructor allows derived classes to initialize a reusable base helper while preventing clients from creating the helper as a standalone object. ClusLib applies this idea to classes whose data and methods are meaningful only as part of Arguments, Results, or a typed container.

The access rule communicates design intent at compile time. It avoids a public object with incomplete semantics while retaining construction reuse for every legitimate subclass.

A protocol data unit is the data passed through a layer of the network stack together with the headers or footers that give that layer's peer enough context to interpret it. Encapsulation adds this context as data moves downward through a sender's stack.

The receiving host removes and interprets the corresponding layer information as the data moves upward. The exact name and fields vary by layer and protocol, but the purpose is to preserve the information required for standardized peer communication.

A proton exchange membrane fuel cell uses a thin polymer [[Fuel Cell Electrolyte]] that passes hydrogen ions while electrons follow the external load. The source describes porous carbon electrodes with platinum catalyst, relatively low operating temperature, high power density, and quick output changes. Those properties suit vehicle propulsion and building supply, but catalyst cost and sensitivity to fuel impurities are practical concerns.

A prototype decision record connects an artifact to the design question it explored, the evidence gathered during play, and the decision made afterward. It prevents the team from remembering only whether a prototype felt successful.

Recording rejected alternatives and remaining uncertainty keeps later iterations from repeating a test without understanding why the earlier result was accepted, revised, or discarded.

A prototype is a representation of a design used to explore, communicate, or evaluate it before the final system is complete. Its fidelity describes how closely and completely it represents the intended result.

Early prototypes can be inexpensive and incomplete when the question concerns layout or flow. A [[3D User Interface]] often requires a more functional prototype because spatial mappings, devices, movement, and sensory feedback are difficult to judge on paper.

Prototypes make imagined details concrete. They support rapid [[Formative Evaluation]], reveal flawed assumptions, and allow repeated design changes before production work is fixed.

For a game, a prototype must include at least one working interactive loop; a static mockup, prerecorded demonstration, or noninteractive simulation does not test gameplay. Each prototype should answer a clear design question, remain separate from production code, and be cheap enough to discard after it informs the next [[Design-Build-Test Loop|iteration]].

In an agile backlog, a timeboxed [[Spike]] can use a prototype to remove uncertainty before estimation or commitment. Prototyping is especially important for novel platforms, where changing hardware constraints make long-range designs assumption-heavy and several parallel options may need to be tested.

A prototype is most useful when it poses a specific question that can be answered through play. Its features and fidelity should be limited to what is necessary to expose that uncertainty.

Treating the artifact as a question prevents polish from masquerading as knowledge. A narrow prototype can be discarded after the answer changes the design, while an unfocused miniature game makes it difficult to know which assumption a test confirmed or challenged.

A proximity matrix is a square table whose cell at row i and column j records the similarity or distance between the corresponding objects. Symmetric measures produce mirrored values around the diagonal, though asymmetric relationships are possible.

Many hierarchical algorithms operate on this matrix rather than the original feature table. It also provides the basis for comparing original relationships with the [[Cophenetic Proximity]] represented by a dendrogram.

A proximity measure quantifies the relationship between two observations or clusters. Similarity measures grow as objects become more alike; dissimilarity measures such as distance grow as they become less alike.

Euclidean, Manhattan, Minkowski, Chebyshev, power, and percent-disagreement measures emphasize different geometry or data types. Since clustering is built on proximity, the chosen measure determines which neighborhoods and shapes an algorithm can recognize.

A pseudo-element styles a portion or generated abstraction that is not an ordinary element in the document tree. Examples include the first formatted line, the first letter, and generated `::before` or `::after` content.

First-line and first-letter styling are constrained to properties that make sense for those fragments. The generated pseudo-elements work with [[CSS Generated Content]] to insert presentational material around an element's content.

A pseudorandom ranging code is a deterministic bit sequence chosen to resemble random noise while remaining exactly reproducible by a receiver. Each satellite uses an identifiable code, allowing several weak signals to occupy the same carrier band with limited mutual interference. The receiver slides a local copy of a code until it correlates with the received sequence. That alignment both identifies the satellite and exposes the signal delay used for ranging.

A public API contract is the explicit data shape accepted or returned at an application boundary. In a web API, strongly typed request [[Data Transfer Object]]s collectively define what outside clients can send without exposing internal domain objects. Contracts favor serializable values and can be versioned independently of a [[Domain Model]]. The [[Application Layer]] converts them into domain-specific values or commands, making transport compatibility a deliberate boundary concern.

A public cloud offers services to the public or to organizations generally, most often through the Internet. A provider pools resources across consumers and commonly charges recurring operating expenditure with little or no consumer capital investment.

Public reach and shared scale can improve convenience and cost flexibility. A consumer must still determine where data may be stored, which legal or regulatory requirements apply, how tenants are isolated, and what happens if the provider becomes unavailable.

A publish profile stores a repeatable set of application publication settings for a destination. Profiles can target a folder, FTP location, or configured virtual machine and select build and deployment options.

Publishing produces the server application and compiled Angular files that the target host will serve. A profile automates the packaging step but does not replace target configuration such as IIS bindings, Nginx rules, or environment values.

Visual Studio's publishing workflow can create or import a profile for Azure App Service, IIS, FTP, Web Deploy, a package, or a folder target. The saved profile makes the selected build and destination settings repeatable while leaving credentials and production configuration as separate concerns.

A pull system starts upstream work in response to available downstream capacity. A stage takes a completed item from the preceding stage when it can work on it, instead of receiving work pushed according to a schedule.

Pull limits queues and makes constraints visible. It works with a [[Work in Progress Limit]] so the system responds to actual flow rather than maximizing local utilization.

A punched card can encode control instructions as well as data. Jacquard looms used hole patterns to select threads, while later computing installations used cards to determine operations and the sequence of jobs.

The distinction between data and control depends on interpretation rather than the physical card. This anticipated the stored-program insight that one encoded pattern may be treated as information or as an instruction.

A punched-card installation combined key punches, sorters, tabulators, and later calculators. Operators encoded records, sorted decks by selected columns, counted or summarized them, and carried results to the next machine.

The workflow performed sophisticated data processing even though no single device was a general computer. Human coordination supplied the program that connected specialized machines.

A punishment is a consequence that signals an action or situation the game discourages. It can increase resistance, remove a resource, give an opponent an advantage, or send the player backward through the experience.

Punishment differs from a rule that merely blocks an action. It changes the player's situation after failure or error, and its design determines how much time, progress, and opportunity the player must lose before trying again.

A pure function produces the same result for the same arguments and has no externally observable side effects. The book's discount calculation depends on price and discount inputs rather than changing inventory state, so it can be tested with ordinary input-output examples. Purity does not prove that the inputs are valid business values; that separate concern can be represented through validation or a constrained input type.

A pure virtual extension point declares a required operation without a base implementation. Concrete clustering classes must supply the operation before they can be instantiated, as linkage subclasses implement distance updates and algorithms implement their computation and result transfer.

The extension point isolates genuine variation while the surrounding base class preserves shared behavior. Too many hooks expose unstable internals, whereas too few force subclasses to duplicate the control flow.

A push notification service accepts a message from an application backend and routes it through the notification system of each target platform. It gives the backend a way to alert a mobile application without maintaining a continuously active application process on the device.

Platform notification services impose different payload and addressing rules. A broker such as Azure Notification Hubs can provide one server-side interface while templates or platform payloads preserve the target-specific delivery requirements.

A pushdown automaton is a finite-state machine augmented by a stack. A transition may consume an input symbol or ε, pop a string from the stack, push a replacement string, and change state.

The stack supplies unbounded last-in-first-out memory for nested structure. Pushdown automata accept exactly the [[Context-Free Language|context-free languages]], and a grammar can be simulated by pushing its start symbol, expanding nonterminals, and matching terminals against the input.

A pyramidal time frame stores stream summaries at multiple temporal resolutions. Recent snapshots are retained densely, while older snapshots are kept at increasingly coarse intervals.

This bounded history supports approximate queries over many user-selected horizons without keeping every update. Temporal accuracy decreases for older periods, making the retention schedule an explicit space-versus-resolution tradeoff.

A Python method table maps exposed method names to C function pointers, call flags, and documentation. Blender assigns such an array to an extension type so the interpreter can dispatch a script call to the matching implementation.

Different flags identify instance, class, argument, or no-argument calling conventions. A sentinel entry containing null fields terminates the table. The [[Blender mathutils Vector Method Dispatch]] demonstrates the mapping, while writable attributes can use a separate [[Blender Python Get-Set Definition]].

A q-value assigns each feature the smallest estimated false discovery rate at which that feature would be included in the selected set. It is a multiple-testing analogue of a p-value tied to discovery-list error rather than one-test null evidence.

Thresholding q-values produces a list with a chosen estimated error rate. The interpretation depends on the underlying [[Null Proportion Estimate]] and false-discovery model used to calculate them.

A quadcopter uses four rotor thrust vectors mounted on a rigid frame. Opposite pairs rotate in opposing directions so their reaction torques can cancel in a steady hover, while total upward thrust balances weight. Changing selected rotor speeds breaks those balances to command the motions in [[Drone Roll, Pitch, and Yaw Control]].

A quadratic equation in one unknown has a squared variable as its highest power and can be written

$$ax^2+bx+c=0,$$

where (a\neq0) and the coefficients are real numbers. The equation may have more than one solution because different numbers can produce the same square.

Common solution methods are [[Solving Quadratics by Factoring]], [[Completing the Square]], and the [[Quadratic Formula]]. Before applying them, simplify the equation and place it in [[Standard Form of a Quadratic Equation]].

A quadratic form is a scalar expression of the form $q(x)=x^TAx$. Only the symmetric part of $A$ affects its value, so it can be represented by a [[Symmetric Matrix]].

The sign of $q(x)$ for nonzero vectors classifies $A$ as positive definite, semidefinite, negative definite, or indefinite. This classification connects eigenvalues and the [[Hessian Matrix]] to curvature and extrema.

A quadratic inequality asks where a quadratic polynomial is positive, negative, nonnegative, or nonpositive. Its real roots divide the [[Real Number Line]] into sign intervals. Testing one point in each interval, or reading the parabola's position relative to the horizontal axis, determines which intervals satisfy the comparison.

A qualitative choropleth fills regions according to nominal categories rather than ordered quantities. Distinct hues should make categories separable without implying that one is larger or better. The number of categories must remain small enough for reliable identification, and adjacent regions need sufficient contrast. If the categories have a natural order, an ordered palette and quantitative mapping may communicate the structure more honestly.

A quantile divides an ordered distribution according to a cumulative probability. Quartiles are quantiles at 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75, while arbitrary probability values yield corresponding [[Percentile|percentiles]].

Quantiles are robust descriptions of position and useful inputs to [[Quantile-Based Grouping]]. Their calculation must specify how missing values are handled, because an unremoved missing value can prevent the estimate or silently change the analyzed subset.

The source presents a quantile as the inverse perspective on a cumulative distribution: a probability identifies the value below which that proportion of observations falls. This relationship makes quantiles useful both for distribution summaries and for constructing a [[Quantile-Quantile Plot]].

A quantile–quantile plot compares the ordered values of a sample with the quantiles expected from a reference distribution, commonly the normal distribution. Points close to the reference line indicate similar distributional shape.

Systematic curvature or departure in the tails suggests that the reference distribution is a poor description. The plot is a diagnostic aid rather than a mechanical pass–fail test, and its interpretation should consider sample size and the intended model.

The source constructs the plot by pairing observed sample percentiles with theoretical normal percentiles. Approximate alignment supports the normal model used by a small-sample t procedure, whereas systematic tail departures warn that the approximation may be unreliable.

A quantitative raster map assigns a color from an ordered scale to each cell's numeric value. It shows the spatial variation of a [[Spatial Field]] at the raster's resolution. A color key must state the value mapping, and boundaries or coastlines can provide context without hiding cells. For multilayer data, shared limits make panels comparable, while [[Raster Marginal Summary|marginal summaries]] can relate the map to aggregated row or column patterns.

A quark is an elementary particle carrying fractional electric charge and participating in the strong interaction. Six flavors occur in three generations. Quarks are confined within composite hadrons: three-quark combinations form baryons such as protons and neutrons, while quark-antiquark pairs form mesons.

A quartz oscillator uses the crystal's piezoelectric resonance as a stable frequency reference. Its rapid, regular vibration permits more precise portable timekeeping than a mechanical balance wheel, which made accurate radio navigation and early satellite transmitters practical. Quartz is not perfectly invariant: temperature, contamination, shock, and aging can shift its frequency, so demanding systems monitor or correct its drift against a better standard.

A quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme is locally obtained from a module by localization. For an A-module M, the associated sheaf assigns M_f to the basic open set D(f).

The source describes an equivalence between A-modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on Spec(A). Module operations can therefore be interpreted as local geometric data over an [[Affine Scheme]].

A quasi-static electromagnetic field varies with time slowly enough, or occurs in a conductor good enough, that displacement current can be neglected relative to conduction current. The remaining equations retain selected time-varying effects without the full wave coupling.

This approximation is useful in conducting media over frequency ranges where charge and current respond much faster than electromagnetic propagation effects. Its validity depends on material and scale.

A query API exposes [[Application Query]] operations separately from state-changing command endpoints. Its routes and response contracts are organized around the information a client needs, such as browsing published items or viewing one item with owner details. The endpoint can return a [[Read Model]] directly and does not route the request through the [[Repository Pattern]] solely to reconstruct a behavioral aggregate. This keeps retrieval concerns independent of aggregate persistence.

A query parameter is a named value encoded after the question mark in a URL. It supplies optional navigation state, such as search criteria, without changing the route's path structure.

A React component reads the location search string and parses its values. The parameter should be encoded when written and treated as untrusted input when it later becomes part of an API request.

A queueing state-space model represents a service system by its possible occupancy states and transitions caused by arrivals and departures. Transition rates determine how probability flows among those states.

Once steady-state occupancies are estimated, designers can calculate throughput, response time, and overflow risk. This permits capacity to be chosen against a target probability of denying service instead of provisioning for every possible demand.

Newton’s Legacy: “The System of the World”
In the late 1600s, Isaac Newton, who was familiar with Descartes’ work and who had almost
certainly read Galileo’s book as it so clearly influenced his own, corresponded with Edmund
Halley (for whom the famous comet is named) about the calculations of comets and the moons
of Jupiter. Halley had kept precise observations of these with his telescope, and Newton used
Halley’s notes in his mathematical modeling. Based on their correspondence (including an
earlier, unpublished paper that we have now only in draft form) and Halley’s observational data,
Isaac Newton was able to make the final argument in favor of Copernicus and the Sun-centered
view of the solar system, and in so doing, he removed geocentrism and Brahe’s model from
serious consideration of how the world worked (Newton c.1687/1974).
Newton did this as part of publishing his master work, the Principia Mathematica, in 1687.
(Newton 1687/c.1846). Book III of the Principia is called De Mundi Systemate, or The System of
the World —an important volume and title. In this volume, Newton derived his now famous
equation describing gravity, based on Halley’s meticulous observations of Jupiter’s moons.
More importantly, he showed that this gravity was the same on Earth and in the heavens. Prior
to this there was no assumption, much less an equation to show, that physical mechanisms
operated the same on Earth as on Jupiter. There was simply no expectation that physical
mechanisms were unified in any way. Newton’s equations showed that there were not many
systems operating, but one…one gravitation, one organizing principle, one system: the system
of the world.
It’s difficult to overstate the importance of Newton’s Principia or the change it brought about in
how people viewed the world. The idea that the path followed by a ball tossed into the air on
Earth can be described by the same equations as the paths of the dimly seen sparks of light that
are the distant moons orbiting Jupiter was more than revolutionary. This idea created a new,
unified, mechanistic view of the universe. The Sun and the planets were all part of an enormous
mechanism that could be fully described mathematically like a giant clockwork.

mathematical discipline, in itself purely formal but applicable to the various empirical sciences…
[including] most diverse fields, such as thermodynamics, biological and medical experimentation,
genetics, life insurance statistics, etc. (Bertalnaffy 1968)
While Bertalanffy was never able to see this vision fulfilled, his work was crucial in spreading the
principles of systems thinking into many disciplines.
During the mid-20th century, others were active in exploring and winnowing concepts that
would lead to broader systems thinking. One notable is Norbert Wiener, who wrote the seminal
book Cybernetics (1948). This mathematically oriented book led to many advances in computer
science, artificial intelligence, and systems thinking. At the same time, its title, focus, and later
influence may be indicative of an important divide in thinking about systems. Cybernetics
comes from the Greek word meaning “governance” or “one who steers or controls.”

A quicksort pivot is the item used to partition a collection during [[Quicksort]]. Items smaller than the pivot move to one side, while items at least as large move to the other, leaving the pivot in its final sorted position.

An extreme pivot such as the current minimum produces a badly unbalanced partition and little progress. Selecting pivots at random avoids spending extra work searching for an ideal pivot while making a long sequence of worst choices exceedingly improbable.

A race condition occurs when a program's result depends on the timing or interleaving of concurrent operations. Unsynchronized read-modify-write sequences can lose updates even when each individual read and write appears simple.

Races are prevented by removing shared mutable state, partitioning ownership, using immutable data, or applying an appropriate synchronization primitive. Tests may fail to reproduce them consistently because scheduling changes from run to run.

The design-patterns source demonstrates that making an inventory context a singleton does not make `Quantity += amount` atomic. Two threads can read the same old quantity and overwrite one another's updates. Locking the read-modify-write section protects that invariant, while constructing the singleton itself needs a separate one-time creation guarantee.

A radial dead zone filters a two-dimensional analog stick according to the magnitude of its vector rather than filtering the horizontal and vertical axes independently. Values inside a central radius become zero.

Values outside the dead zone are rescaled so movement reaches full magnitude near the hardware limit. This preserves circular direction behavior and avoids the square or cross-shaped response created by separate axis thresholds.

A radial gradient changes color outward from a center through circular or elliptical rings. Its size can be given explicitly or selected with keywords that reach a chosen side or corner of the gradient box.

Repeating linear and radial gradients repeat the color-stop pattern after the final stop, producing stripes, rings, or other tiled effects without a separate image file. The interval between the first and last effective stops defines the repeated period.

A radial popularity coordinate places more popular or higher-degree network nodes closer to the center of a hyperbolic embedding. Newer or less connected nodes are positioned farther outward, and radial movement can represent popularity fading over time.

Because node degree and density vary exponentially with radius, radial position compactly expresses hierarchy and influence. It works with the [[Angular Similarity Coordinate]] to determine hyperbolic proximity.

A radiative view factor is the fraction of energy leaving one surface that reaches another. It is determined by surface area, orientation, separation, visibility, and shadowing rather than by the surfaces' temperatures or material properties.

Convex exterior surfaces cannot see one another in the same way that concave interior surfaces can. [[Surface-to-Surface Radiation|radiation models]] integrate angular contributions over all mutually visible surfaces so that geometric exposure and occlusion are represented in the energy exchange.

A radical ideal is an [[Ideal]] I satisfying I = √I. If a power rⁿ belongs to a radical ideal, then r already belongs to it.

Because the [[Radical of an Ideal]] is the intersection of all [[Prime Ideal]]s containing that ideal, radical ideals record which prime components occur while ignoring their multiplicities. Vanishing ideals of affine algebraic sets are radical in the classical setting developed by the source.

A radio time signal distributes a common clock reference to distant receivers. Ships and aircraft could use broadcasts such as WWV to set chronometers without physically transporting a clock. High-frequency signals traveled far by reflecting from the ionosphere, but changing propagation paths introduced timing uncertainty. Satellite navigation preserves the idea of broadcast time while using higher-frequency signals and explicit corrections for propagation delay.

A radioactive tracer is an isotope incorporated into a biologically active substance so its distribution can be detected outside the body. The tracer should emit sufficiently penetrating radiation, have a half-life long enough for the procedure but short enough to limit dose, and participate in the process under investigation without substantially altering it.

A radiographic image records spatial variation in transmitted X-ray intensity after the beam passes through the body. Differences in thickness, density, and attenuation coefficient create contrast. Lower photon energy can improve contrast but increases absorption and dose, while scatter degrades the image; filtration, collimation, and contrast media manage these tradeoffs.

A random data partition assigns observations to training, validation, and test subsets using random selection. Randomization reduces systematic allocation bias when records are exchangeable.

Class imbalance, grouped observations, or time order may require stratified, grouped, or temporal splitting instead of unrestricted sampling.

A random system produces outcomes that are not determined in advance, although they may fall within a defined probability range. Its unpredictability comes from chance rather than from sensitivity in a deterministic rule set.

This distinguishes it from a [[Chaotic System]]. Games use [[Randomization]] to stand in for systems that are too detailed to model and to introduce uncertainty into [[Meaningful Decision|meaningful decisions]].

A random variable assigns a numerical value to the outcome of a random process. Its realized value changes across repeated samples or experiments even when the underlying population and procedure remain fixed.

The source treats sample means, mean differences, test statistics, and p-values as random variables. Recognizing this variability is essential because an observed estimate is one realization from a [[Sampling Distribution]], not the population quantity itself.

A randomized algorithm deliberately uses chance when selecting part of its execution path. Its result or runtime can vary between runs even when the input is unchanged.

Randomness can avoid consistently unfavorable deterministic choices. [[Quicksort]] selects pivots randomly so that its expected complexity is loglinear, even though a theoretically possible sequence of extreme pivots would be much slower. Correct sorting is guaranteed; chance affects performance rather than correctness.

A rare event Poisson approximation replaces a [[Binomial Distribution]] with a [[Poisson Distribution]] when the number of trials is large, the success probability is small, and their product remains a moderate expected count.

The approximation captures the asymmetric distribution near zero that a normal approximation cannot represent well. Its Poisson rate equals the binomial expected count, preserving the relevant event scale while simplifying calculation.

A raster attribute table associates integer raster cell codes with category labels and possibly additional class attributes. It lets a [[Categorical Raster Map]] display meaningful names instead of raw numbers and supports selecting a qualitative palette by class. The table does not change cell geometry; it supplies semantics for stored values. Codes, labels, and colors should remain synchronized when classes are merged or reordered.

A raster map animation plots each layer of a time-indexed raster with the same graphical settings and concatenates the resulting image files into a movie. It can reveal movement of a continuous field, such as forecast cloud cover, when adjacent layers change smoothly. Administrative boundaries supply fixed spatial context. Inconsistent scales or extents would turn frame-to-frame changes in rendering into apparent changes in the data.

A raster marginal summary aggregates cell values along rows or columns and plots the result beside a [[Quantitative Raster Map]]. It reveals broad variation by latitude or longitude that may be difficult to isolate in the full two-dimensional pattern. The summary function may be a mean, median, or another statistic, and missing cells must be handled consistently. Margins reduce spatial detail, so they complement rather than replace the map.

A rate written as a quotient must convert numerator and denominator in positions that leave the target units. For example, a volume-per-day value needs a volume ratio and a day-to-second ratio oriented inversely because time sits below the fraction line. Pryor's flow, velocity, power, and fuel-efficiency examples all use this same unit algebra even though their physical meanings differ. Checking cancellation prevents a factor of 60 or 3,600 from being accidentally applied in the wrong direction. See [[Conversion-Factor Chains]].

A rater policy is the functional relationship a judge appears to use when converting a profile of predictor values into an overall decision. Judgmental analysis represents that relationship through a multiple-regression equation.

Comparing equations reveals whether judges share a policy even when their individual ratings differ. The result preserves both the direction and relative importance of the predictors.

A rational exponent connects powers and roots: $a^{m/n}=(\sqrt[n]{a})^m$ when the real root is defined. The denominator selects the root and the numerator selects the power. These definitions extend the [[Exponent Laws]], but even roots impose nonnegative-radicand restrictions when calculations remain in the real numbers.

A rational expression is a quotient of algebraic expressions, commonly polynomials:

$$\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)},\qquad Q(x)\neq0.$$

It generalizes a numerical [[Fraction]] while retaining the restriction that its denominator cannot be zero. Operations follow fraction rules, but polynomial factorization is often required before cancellation or construction of a common denominator. Equivalent-looking simplified forms must preserve the original excluded values because cancelling a factor does not make the original denominator defined there.

A rational expression is undefined at any value that makes its denominator zero. Before simplifying

$$\frac{x^2-1}{x-1},$$

the value (x=1) must be excluded. Factoring and cancelling gives (x+1), but the original expression still has no value at (x=1).

Restrictions should therefore be identified before cancellation, multiplication, or cross multiplication. A transformation can preserve equality only on the domain where every expression and division used in the step is defined.

A rational function is a quotient $f(x)=p(x)/q(x)$ of polynomials with $q(x)\ne0$. Zeros of the denominator are excluded from its domain and may produce holes or [[Vertical Asymptote]]s. Comparing polynomial degrees helps determine end behavior and possible [[Horizontal Asymptote]]s.

A rational inequality compares a [[Rational Expression]] with zero or another expression. Zeros of the numerator and denominator divide the number line into sign intervals, but denominator zeros are always excluded. A sign chart avoids unsafe cross-multiplication by a quantity whose sign may be unknown.

A rational number is a number expressible as a quotient of two integers,

$$\frac{a}{b},\qquad b\neq0.$$

Rational numbers include integers and positive or negative [[Fraction]]s. They are closed under addition, subtraction, and multiplication, and under division by a nonzero rational number. In positional decimal notation, every rational number has an expansion that either terminates or eventually repeats. Conversely, a terminating or [[Repeating Decimal]] represents a rational number.

A raw attribute is recorded directly from a source; a derived attribute is calculated from other fields. Derivation can encode a meaningful interaction that no single raw field expresses. The book uses body mass index, calculated from weight and height, to illustrate how a combined measure may relate more strongly to a study target than either input alone.

Derived features still need domain scrutiny. A useful calculation for one setting may be unhelpful elsewhere, and an inappropriate transformation can hide differences. Feature design is part of representing the problem, not just a technical optimization after data collection.

A raw Ethernet storage protocol places storage-specific messages directly in Ethernet frames instead of passing every request through a full general-purpose network stack. The shorter path can reduce processing, copies, and latency for small I/O.

The protocol must supply any required reliability, addressing, flow control, and request matching that higher layers would otherwise provide.

A Razor layout defines the shared outer structure of multiple pages or views, such as navigation, metadata, scripts, and a common visual shell. Each content page supplies its body and may define named sections consumed by the layout.

Layouts reduce duplicated markup and create a single place for application-wide presentation changes. Shared view imports and startup files can further establish common namespaces, tag helpers, and default layout choices.

A Razor Page pairs a `.cshtml` template with an optional page-model class that contains request handlers, bound properties, and presentation logic. Handler methods correspond to HTTP operations and can prepare the data rendered by the page.

The page-centered structure keeps the code for one screen close together while still separating C# behavior from markup. Services supplied through dependency injection let the page model coordinate persistence or application logic without constructing its dependencies directly.

A React component prop is an input passed from a consuming component to a child component. Props make a component configurable in the same way that function parameters make a function reusable.

TypeScript interfaces can specify prop names and types, including callback functions. A component reads its props when rendering but does not treat them as its own mutable state.

A React element is an object describing what should appear at one position in the interface tree. JSX expressions produce these element descriptions for intrinsic browser elements or for other React components.

Elements are descriptions rather than mutable document nodes. React compares the newly produced tree with the prior rendering and applies the required browser updates.

A React form coordinates controlled field values, validation state, submission progress, and success or failure behavior. The browser form event is handled by component logic so the application can validate and send data without an automatic page navigation.

Reusable form and field components reduce repeated state and event code. Server-side validation remains necessary even when the React form provides complete client feedback.

A React Router Link renders navigable content that changes the client-side location without forcing a full document request. It preserves browser navigation behavior while letting the router select the destination component.

Links are appropriate when navigation is part of rendered content. An event handler that decides a destination after work completes can use [[Programmatic Navigation]] instead.

A reactive assistant acts in response to an explicit user request or event. The user initiates the exchange, so the immediate purpose of the interaction is comparatively clear.

Reactive behavior limits interruption and privacy risks, but it cannot surface useful information before the user thinks to ask. A [[Proactive Assistant]] takes the stronger step of initiating an interaction.

A reactive stream is a time-ordered sequence of notifications. It may emit values, report an error, and signal completion, so a consumer must consider more than the next ordinary value. User events, inventory updates, and calculated totals can each be treated as streams. Operators can derive new streams without requiring producers to know every downstream consumer.

A reactive system is an architectural arrangement designed to remain responsive under changing load and partial failure. The book describes responsiveness, scalability, resilience, and message-based communication as its related properties. This is broader than using an observable sequence inside one process: component boundaries, resource allocation, and failure isolation determine whether the whole service can keep responding.

A read model is a data representation shaped for a specific information need. An [[Application Query]] retrieves it without invoking state-changing domain behavior, and the API can often return the stored shape directly without mapping it through an [[Aggregate]]. Read models can combine fields from several aggregates and use indexes or denormalization suited to their consumers. In event-sourced systems, a [[Projection]] builds and updates them from domain events.

A real number is any [[Rational Number]] or [[Irrational Number]]. The real numbers fill the [[Number Line]]: each point corresponds to a real value, and order corresponds to position from left to right.

Elementary algebra generally treats variables as real unless another domain is specified. The real-number system supports addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by nonzero values, along with order comparisons. Restrictions still matter; for example, a denominator cannot equal zero, and an even root is not a real number when its radicand is negative.

A real square matrix $Q$ is orthogonal when $Q^TQ=QQ^T=I$, so $Q^{-1}=Q^T$. Its columns and rows form orthonormal sets.

Orthogonal transformations preserve vector lengths and angles. This makes them numerically valuable in [[QR Decomposition]], [[Orthogonal Diagonalization]], [[Givens Rotation]], and [[Householder Transformation]].

A real square matrix is skew-symmetric when $A^T=-A$. Every diagonal entry must therefore be zero.

The condition is checked by comparing corresponding entries across the main diagonal: $a_{ij}=-a_{ji}$. This distinguishes skew symmetry from the mirrored equality of a [[Symmetric Matrix]].

A real square matrix is symmetric when $A^T=A$. Its entries mirror across the main diagonal.

Symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues and admit an orthonormal set of eigenvectors, enabling [[Orthogonal Diagonalization]]. They also arise as [[Hessian Matrix|Hessian matrices]], normal-equation matrices, and positive-definite coefficient matrices.

A real symmetric matrix $A$ is positive definite when $x^TAx>0$ for every nonzero vector $x$. Its eigenvalues are positive.

Positive definiteness guarantees important numerical behavior: [[Cholesky Decomposition]] exists, the [[Conjugate Gradient Method]] has a suitable energy minimization interpretation, and a positive-definite [[Hessian Matrix]] identifies a strict local minimum.

A real-time API allows the server to deliver an event to a client without waiting for that client to poll another request. It is useful when the value of a screen changes because of activity elsewhere in the system.

The contract defines connection setup as well as message names and payloads. Clients must map each message into their own state and remain prepared for connection failure or interruption.

A receiver operating characteristic curve plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate as the decision threshold of a probabilistic binary classifier varies. Each point represents a different discrete operating rule.

Curves toward the upper-left indicate stronger separation, and the area under the curve summarizes ranking performance across thresholds. Operational selection still requires a specific balance between missed positives and false alarms.

The book uses ROC curves to compare predictive models across possible probability cutoffs rather than fixing one threshold prematurely. It pairs the curve with area under the curve and risk-oriented displays that connect ranking quality to use.

A recently popular method of an fMRI experiment, known as resting state fMRI (rs-fMRI),
involves measuring blood oxygenation while not performing any explicit task. This method was
first described by Biswal et al. [13], in which he explored the relationships between brain regions
rather than the application of explicit tasks to find regions associated with those tasks.
The signal strength in fMRI is low and requires elaborate processing to be able to extract use-
ful information from the recorded data from an MR machine. Similar to any measurement system,
there is system noise in the recorded signal. This includes thermal noise, RF-induced noise, noise
introduced while signal amplification and other system-related processes that cause system insta-
bility. In addition to the system noise, there is also a physiological noise induced by changes in the
physiology of the human (or animal) subject. This includes noise introduced due to motion (of the
human) during scanning, signal fluctuations induced by cardiac pulsation, signal fluctuations due
to magnetic field change induced by the amount of air in the lungs (respiration), and fluctuations
in hematocrit content in the blood that influences the magnetic properties of the tissue and several
others. While it is difficult to entirely eliminate noise, the attempt is to maximize sensitivity and
specificity by reducing the effects of noise.

A receptive field is the limited region of an input image inspected by one neuron in a [[Convolutional Neural Network]]. Early convolutional neurons take values from small neighboring pixel patches rather than the whole image. Neurons that share a detector can be placed at different positions, so their receptive fields collectively search for the same local feature across the image.

Neighboring fields may overlap. Their separation is controlled by [[Convolutional Stride]]. Later layers can combine responses from multiple local fields into features with broader spatial scope. The field is therefore an architectural choice about which input relationships a neuron can use directly.

A recommender system predicts or ranks items that may be useful to a user from observed preferences, item information, or interactions. Its output reduces a large choice space to a personalized set of candidates.

Different systems rely on [[Collaborative Filtering]], [[Content-Based Recommendation]], or a hybrid. The appropriate design depends on available feedback, scale, changing context, and how recommendation quality will be evaluated.

A record exclusion audit preserves or counts observations removed by each filtering rule. Instead of viewing exclusion as a silent side effect, the analyst records why rows left the analysis and how many were affected.

The audit can reveal selection bias, especially when a required measure is missing for most people with the outcome. It also supports rollback and verification by showing that retained and excluded partitions reconcile with the input dataset.

Removing observations with a missing target is a consequential modeling decision in the book's preparation workflow. Recording the affected rows and counts distinguishes a justified analytic population from an accidental loss of data.

A recovery point objective is the maximum targeted age of data that may be lost when a system is restored after disruption. It describes how far back in time the recovered state may be compared with the moment of failure.

The objective determines how frequently data must be replicated or backed up. It is distinct from [[Recovery Time Objective]], which measures the acceptable duration of the outage rather than the acceptable amount of lost history.

A recovery time objective is the maximum targeted interval between a service disruption and restoration of usable service. It answers how long the organization can tolerate the affected system remaining unavailable.

The objective should appear in continuity planning and service commitments so recovery capability can be designed and tested. A short recovery time may require ready secondary capacity, automation, and practiced failover rather than relying only on stored backups.

A rectangular matrix has a different number of rows and columns. An $m\times n$ matrix is rectangular when $m\neq n$.

Rectangular coefficient matrices naturally describe [[Overdetermined Linear System|overdetermined]] and [[Underdetermined Linear System|underdetermined]] systems. They do not have ordinary two-sided inverses, but a [[Pseudoinverse]] and [[Least Squares Approximation]] can supply useful generalized solutions.

A recurrence trigger starts a logic app on a repeated schedule. The campaign workflow uses it to check an Excel table at a chosen interval for rows whose intended publication time has arrived.

A shorter interval makes the automation more responsive but causes more workflow executions. Scheduling is therefore both a behavior decision and an operational-cost decision, even when most runs discover no work.

A recurrent network carries a vector of hidden-layer activations from one sequence step into the next. At the current step, the hidden layer receives both the new input and this stored context. Its output is used to produce the current result and to update the state for the following step.

The memory buffer in Kelleher's [[Recurrent Neural Network]] diagram stores activations without transforming them; weighted connections from the buffer to the hidden units perform the next transformation. This feedback lets a later input be processed in the context of earlier inputs, although basic recurrence can struggle to retain long-range information during training.

A recurrent neural network processes a sequence while carrying information from earlier steps into later ones. Its recurrent connections make the current output depend on both the present input and a representation of prior inputs.

This structure fits speech and language, where word or sound interpretation depends on surrounding sequence context. [[Long Short-Term Memory]] units were developed to preserve relevant information across longer spans.

Kelleher depicts the network's [[Recurrent Hidden State|hidden state]] as a memory buffer whose activations are fed into the next step along with its new input. [[Time-Unrolled Recurrent Network|Unrolling]] the loop shows how one set of [[Recurrent Weight Sharing Across Time|shared recurrent weights]] is reused through a sequence. Training with [[Backpropagation Through Time]] then has to propagate error through those steps, which can make long-range dependencies difficult to learn.

A recursive belief update uses the posterior from one step as the prior for the next. A repeated transition-and-observation decomposition prevents the full observation history from having to be reconsidered from scratch.

The same description can answer filtering, prediction, or smoothing questions by changing the time index of the searched state. Its efficiency comes from the Markov assumptions encoded in the decomposition.

A recursive definition specifies initial values and then defines later or larger objects in terms of earlier or smaller ones. The factorial definition fixes 0! = 1 and defines n! = n(n − 1)! for n > 0; the Fibonacci sequence requires two initial values before applying its recurrence.

Because the definition builds an infinite family from finite rules, facts about recursively defined objects are commonly proved with [[Mathematical Induction]] or [[Strong Induction]].

A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler input. It requires a base case that returns without another call and a recursive case that makes progress toward that base.

Each call consumes stack space until it returns, so missing or unreachable termination can cause a stack overflow. Recursive definitions can closely match problems such as factorials, but their numeric result can still overflow the chosen return type even when the recursion itself terminates correctly.

A recursive graph feature repeatedly aggregates features from neighboring nodes. Starting with basic properties, each iteration expands the represented context to another graph radius.

This construction can create expressive relational features without naming every motif. Repeated aggregation may blur distinct nodes into similar representations, so depth, aggregation functions, and pruning matter.

A recursive language is a synonym for a [[Turing-Decidable Language]]. Membership is determined by a computation that always halts with either acceptance or rejection.

A language is recursive exactly when both it and its complement are [[Recursively Enumerable Language|recursively enumerable]]. Running their accepting machines in alternating steps guarantees that one halts and reveals the correct decision for each input.

A recursively enumerable language can be listed by a machine that runs indefinitely, eventually outputting every member and no nonmember. The order need not be fixed, and repetitions are allowed.

This class is equivalent to the [[Turing-Acceptable Language|Turing-acceptable languages]], the ranges of Turing-computable enumerating functions, and the languages generated by general grammars. Dovetailing several simulations prevents one nonhalting computation from blocking all later candidates.

A red-cyan anaglyph combines the red channel from one eye view with the green and blue channels from the other. Correspondingly colored filters then present the intended channel combination to each eye. The book demonstrates the assembly by disabling green and blue in the left image layer and red in the right layer. This is a presentation method for a stereo pair, not a way to invent depth from a single identical view. The two viewpoints must first satisfy [[Left- and Right-Eye Image Separation]].

A reduced ring is a ring whose [[Nilradical]] is zero. Equivalently, it has no nonzero [[Nilpotent Element]]s.

Every ring R has a canonical reduced quotient R/N, where N is its nilradical. This quotient preserves the prime-ideal structure while eliminating elements whose powers vanish.

A Redux action creator is a function that constructs an action. Centralizing this construction gives calling code a stable operation and keeps action types and payload shapes from being repeated throughout components.

A synchronous action creator returns an action immediately. With middleware such as Redux Thunk, an action creator can instead coordinate asynchronous work and dispatch later actions as that work progresses.

A Redux action is an object that describes an event that may change application state. Its type identifies what happened, and additional fields carry the data the reducer needs to interpret that event.

Actions describe requested transitions without performing them. Dispatching the action sends it through the store to the reducer, which decides the resulting state.

A Redux provider places the store into React's component context so descendants can access it without passing the store through every intermediate prop. It normally wraps the application near the root of the component tree.

The provider supplies access, while connected components or hooks choose which state and dispatch operations they consume. This keeps the store shared without making every component depend on its entire contents.

A Redux reducer is a pure function that receives the current state and an action and returns the next state. It expresses how each recognized event transforms the store without mutating the existing state object.

Keeping reducers deterministic makes state changes easier to reason about and test. An unrecognized action returns the current state, preserving the store when no transition applies.

A Redux store holds the application's shared state tree and coordinates access to it. It exposes the current state, accepts dispatched actions, and notifies subscribers after the reducer has produced a new state.

The store is the meeting point between action-producing code and state-consuming UI. React components normally receive it through a provider instead of importing a mutable global value.

A reference frame establishes what positions, orientations, and movements are measured relative to.

An egocentric frame is relative to the user's body, such as the eyes, head, torso, hands, or legs, and corresponds to a first-person view. An exocentric frame is relative to an object or the world and corresponds to an outside or third-person view.

In a [[3D User Interface]], changing between egocentric and exocentric views can help different tasks but may also confuse the user. [[Navigation]], [[System Control]], and [[3D Manipulation]] should use a frame that makes their mappings easy to predict.

A reference map helps locate named geographic features such as roads, settlements, boundaries, and landmarks. Its purpose is orientation rather than emphasizing one statistical variable. Web tiles can supply this context beneath a thematic layer, provided the thematic data are transformed to the tile system. Excess detail competes with symbols, so reference content should be selected according to scale and the locations readers need to recognize.

A reflective choice asks the player to consider values, identity, or attitude even though the selected option does not change the plot or game state. Its purpose is to focus attention on the act of choosing and on what that choice means to the player.

Because meaning can arise from interpretation rather than only from mechanical consequence, a reflective choice may affect the experience without altering the outcome. It can ask who the player or character is within the story when no decision can produce a perfect result.

A regenerative fuel-cell arrangement uses available energy to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, then later combines those gases in a [[Fuel Cell]] to make electricity and water again. This makes the reactants a way to store energy across time, rather than a one-way fuel feed. The source illustrates sunlight driving the splitting step, with produced water recirculated for another cycle.

A regional health data platform integrates healthcare information across institutions within a geographic area. It can connect hospital, primary-care, public-health, and administrative records for broader management and analysis.

Integration improves continuity and population-level insight, but it also concentrates sensitive information. Shared definitions, access controls, legal authority, and accountability are necessary for the platform to be trustworthy.

A regression interaction term represents a relationship in which the effect of one explanatory variable depends on the level of another. It is commonly formed as a product while retaining the corresponding lower-order terms.

Once an interaction is included, the lower-order coefficients cannot be interpreted as universal effects. Estimates become stratum-specific combinations of coefficients, so unplanned interaction searches can both inflate false positives and make the model difficult to communicate.

The source constructs interaction columns by multiplying existing design-matrix columns. In R formula syntax, `type:leg` adds only the product terms, while `type*leg` expands to both main effects and their interaction.

A regression reference group is the category against which indicator-variable coefficients are interpreted. Its observations receive zero on every indicator representing the other levels of the same categorical variable.

Choosing a plausible low-risk or otherwise meaningful group can make coefficients easier to explain. Unknown values sometimes remain in the reference group for practical reasons, but doing so changes its meaning and should be disclosed in the model presentation.

The source shows that R's design matrix omits one factor level and places its fitted mean in the intercept. Coefficients for the remaining levels then represent differences from this reference, so changing the reference changes individual coefficient meanings without changing the fitted group means.

A regression residual plot graphs [[Residual|residuals]] against fitted values, predictors, or theoretical quantiles. A well-specified linear model should not leave an obvious trend or systematic change in residual spread.

Curvature can indicate violation of the [[Linearity Assumption]], while a funnel shape suggests nonconstant variance. Quantile–quantile residual plots assess distributional shape, and unusual isolated points may warrant investigation for data errors or influence.

A regular expression is built from ∅, ε, alphabet symbols, union, concatenation, [[Kleene Star]], and grouping. It generates a [[Formal Language]] by interpreting those constructors as the corresponding operations on sets of strings.

A language is regular when some regular expression generates it. Practical search patterns add conveniences such as character classes, optional items, and one-or-more repetition, but features such as backreferences can exceed the power of formal regular expressions.
